newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to provide rice funds to flood-stricken Laos.
newsitem.headline: Japan to provide rice funds to flood-stricken Laos.

text.p: The Japanese government has agreed to provide up to 500 million yen to Laos on the condition that the flood-stricken country uses the money to buy rice from Japan, Japanese officials said on Tuesday.
Laos will use the funds to buy rice from Japan's domestic grain stocks, the officials said. Japanese and Thai rice will be shipped to Laos by Japanese trade houses, they said.
"The funds will enable Laos to buy nearly 10,000 tonnes of rice. We have no clear idea on when the shipment will be carried out," a Foreign Ministry official said.

In November, the Japanese government announced it would donate more than 60,000 tonnes of rice, including Japanese and foreign rice, to poor countries in Africa, Asia and Central America in a move to reduce its swollen grain stocks.
But this angered foreign rice exporters, such as the United States, which said the move would violate the spirit of the 1993 GATT Uruguay Round agreement.
In Laos, rice crops in key southern growing areas were devastated by severe floods earlier this year, and United Nations relief agency officials have called for emergency food assistance.
